text: I asked a robot arm to hand me a knife. [pause] It put the blade right on my hand.
So I built Sentinel. A rule-based safety layer between the action planner, Muse Spark LLM, and the robot arm. The model decides how. Sentinel decides whether.

LLMs can plan robot actions, but they can't see the danger. [pause] Germany: a factory arm killed a worker. [pause] New Jersey: a warehouse robot gassed twenty-four workers. [pause] California: a security robot ran over a toddler.
So how do we trust robots? [pause] The answer is Sentinel: it works with the robot to stop unsafe actions.
Now let me show you how it works. This is a kitchen in simulation, in MuJoCo. SAM tags every item: what's sharp, liquid, electronic.

You give an instruction. Before the task completes or the arm moves, Sentinel checks every step against fixed rules in memory. No AI call, so it's fast: under 100 milliseconds, and returns a verdict. If a step fails, the planner makes new steps, until every step passes.

And Sentinel keeps learning from memory, so the rules stay accurate. Past runs become new rules. It sees the room as a graph, updated on every move. Sentinel only gives four verdicts: ALLOW, ASK, BLOCK, HALT.

Let me show you. Demo one: pass me the knife. Same request, same model. On the left, no Sentinel: the blade comes as is. On the right, the same plan runs through Sentinel: it turns the handle toward the person, and slows down near them.
Demo two: pour some water. The cup is right by a laptop. Without Sentinel, it just pours. [pause] With Sentinel, round one is blocked, the planner is told to move the cup, and round two pours safely.
Sentinel tracks where every instruction came from. You asked it to tidy up. The note asked it to give the knife to a stranger. Instructions from the room don't count, so it's blocked.

The model alone carried out sixty percent of unsafe plans. Just blocking: thirty. The full loop: nineteen. Blocking alone isn't enough. The loop guides the plan to safety. And safe tasks still succeed about as often: eighty-two percent, versus eighty-three without it.
To test Sentinel in action, visit the link in the description. [pause] Give the robot any instruction, and watch it run twice: [pause] without Sentinel, and with it, side by side.
Sentinel checks every plan, before the robot can run an unsafe instruction.
